preamble: Debuccalization of the velar nasal [ŋ] to a glottal stop [ʔ], with loss of both the velar closure and nasality. In Northern Samoyedic (Nenets and Enets) Proto-Samoyedic word-final *ŋ became a glottal stop, while Nganasan, Selkup and Kamassian kept the nasal; in Tundra Nenets the resulting 'nasal' glottal stop still alternates with a nasal in sandhi. Independently, Tahitian turned Proto-Polynesian *ŋ into [ʔ] in all positions, merging it with the reflex of *k.

examples.note: Final *ŋ became a glottal stop; Forest Nenets няӈ, Nganasan ӈаӈ and Kamassian аӈ keep the nasal.
The old lative suffix *-ŋ surfaces as a glottal stop; Mator куӈа keeps the nasal.

examples.to: Forest Enets наʼ (naʔ), Tundra Enets эʼ (eʔ)
examples.note: Same final *ŋ > ʔ as in Nenets.
Medial *ŋ became the glottal stop ʻeta; cf. Māori and Tongan tangata, Samoan tagata with [ŋ].
Same change; cf. Māori and Rarotongan rangi, Tongan langi.
